question: What does Phenotypic Age Acceleration (PhenoAgeAccel) tell you about a person?
answers: Whether they appear physiologically older (positive) or younger (negative) than expected for their chronological age

receipt.quote: Therefore, PhenoAgeAccel represents Phenotypic Age after accounting for chronological age (i.e., whether a person appears older [positive value] or younger [negative value] than expected, physiologically, based on his/her age).

question: How does Phenotypic Age Acceleration relate to the number of coexisting diseases a person has, among people of the same age?
answers: It tends to rise with disease count: the more coexisting diseases, the phenotypically older the person appears based on clinical biomarkers

receipt.quote: Despite relatively small sample sizes, in general, PhenoAgeAccel appeared to increase as a function of disease count, suggesting that among persons of the same age, the more coexisting diseases a person has, the phenotypically older he/she appears—based on clinical biomarkers.

question: Phenotypic Age predicted all-cause mortality even among disease-free, healthy adults. What does this suggest about what it measures?
answers: It is not simply a measure of disease; it may track the effect of ageing before diseases become clinically evident

receipt.quote: Conversely, in this study, we were able to show that Phenotypic Age was predictive of all-cause mortality among disease-free, healthy adults across the age spectrum. This suggests that Phenotypic Age is not simply a measure of disease or morbidity and instead may be a marker that tracks the effect of aging before diseases become clinically evident.
